A study on stick-slip dynamics of systems governed by Coulomb friction, driven by time-varying forces, is conducted within a mathematical framework. The behavior of these systems, when modeled using regularization techniques, is examined as a parameter approaches its ideal limit. The behavior of the limiting system is characterized and determined under broad conditions, including the integration of oscillatory effects in control laws to enhance understanding.

A recent paper on deep reinforcement learning introduced an innovative approach to risk-sensitive reinforcement learning by integrating future value predictions into the Bellman equation, developed under the framework of probabilistic duality. This study builds upon that work by introducing a robust optimization problem that effectively generalizes probability distributions, enabling the handling of continuous state and action spaces. This problem can be solved efficiently using gradient-based methods, and the linear Wassertone equation provides a computationally efficient solution. Empirical evaluations have demonstrated the method's effectiveness in minimizing both the mean and median of the estimated future value distribution.

In today's digital landscape, digital recommender systems play a crucial role in facilitating user interactions. These systems, particularly those designed for e-commerce, recommend items tailored to each user's preferences. However, incorporating users' past interactions in order is vital for accurate recommendations, especially when items are closely related in the system's item-space. To address this, sequential recommender systems have emerged as a leading approach, utilizing sequences of user interactions to estimate the probability of the next item they might engage with. Notably, most current sequential recommender systems primarily focus on minimizing this probability, often disregarding the underlying user motivations driving their interactions. This research aims to develop a novel, intent-aware sequential recommender system that learns and utilizes users' implicit motivations to make recommendations. By employing a neural network to model user interactions as observable interactions conditioned on the users' motivations, we create a unified, pre-training and fine-tuning framework for this purpose. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first sequential recommender system to explicitly factor in user motivations, and we demonstrate its efficacy through comprehensive experiments on real-world datasets, showcasing its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.

The reducible double confluent Heun equation stands out as a specialized form of the double confluent Heun equation, with significant relevance in the fields of scattering theory and integrable systems. This study, focusing on the reducible DCHE, develops an analytical solution framework that also reveals a broader method for solving a generalized primary equation. Moreover, it anually expands a system of ordinary differential equations derived by Birkhoff and Rosenblum, illustrating how solutions to this system can be represented as Weyl group orbits under Heun transformations. This approach also identifies conditions for generating distinct solutions and establishes a link between the solutions of the generalized primary equation and the standard double confluent Heun equation. Consequently, the solutions of the reducible DCHE can be transformed into the general double confluent Heun equation. Furthermore, the study identifies three types of singularities in the potential of the corresponding scattering problem, with the anharmonic oscillator case exhibiting only a single type of singularity.

Low-rank matrix recovery has been the subject of extensive research in various fields.
This work addresses the problem of estimating a rank-one positive semi-definite matrix from vectors drawn from a Gaussian distribution, where means are correlated but have differing variances.
The primary focus of this work is to establish the statistical and computational limits of exact estimation under the $\ell_1$ loss, considering the possibility of phase transition.
To achieve optimal estimation, a new iterative method is proposed using continuous optimization techniques, which converges quadratically under certain conditions.
To overcome computational limitations, an efficient method is developed to identify key parameters and prove global convergence of the estimator.
To validate theoretical findings, comprehensive simulations are performed.

In the realm of topological phenomena, a notable trend has been observed where traditional concepts of symmetry play a pivotal role, often resulting in protected states and phenomena. This underscores the notion that symmetry serves as a fundamental organizing principle within condensed matter systems. However, this perspective may not be universally applicable. We challenge this idea by presenting an example of topologically distinct states within a two-dimensional system that lacks any form of symmetry. This distinct intrinsic topological phase is characterized by inherent properties, including zero-energy bulk states that emerge from a bulk band inversion. Notably, when this bulk inversion is slightly reversed, it gives rise to resilient edge modes. Moreover, this distinct intrinsic phase can be paired with an extrinsic mechanism, resulting in a robust one-way edge state that persists even in the absence of symmetry. This can be achieved by introducing a staggered sublattice potential along with a non-reciprocal hopping term. These findings suggest that novel topological phenomena may arise in systems that feature both intrinsic and extrinsic mechanisms.

We suggest using the ratio of semi-inclusive to inclusive Lepton Flavor Universality ratios as a precise tool to study flavor and lepton flavor violations in $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ processes. The inclusion ratio is robust against theoretical uncertainties from $b$-hadron decay modes and cancels out common short-distance physics. The included lepton pairs, such as $e^+e^-$ and $\mu^+\mu^-$, can be easily identified with current detector technology. We calculate the included lepton pair ratios in the limit of massless lepton pairs and include the impact of finite particle energies. The ratio's sensitivity to the relevant Wilson coefficients is demonstrated through numerical analysis, and the expected measurement accuracy is estimated.

This study presents a novel, fully decentralized approach to designing distributed Model Predictive Control laws for interconnected systems linked through a communication network. Unlike previous methods, which often rely on intricate, centralized processes, our approach leverages a decentralized optimization technique that accommodates various communication topologies, including lines, rings, grids, and complete networks. This allows for flexible communication requirements, minimal coordination, and efficient handling of state and control constraints. Notably, our method accommodates missing state information through the use of local state estimators. Experimental results, both simulated and real-world, demonstrate the scalability and robustness of our design approach, which also enables the development of a distributed algorithm for simultaneous design and coordination of MPC laws and state estimators, facilitating plug-and-play distributed control implementation.

The COVID19 pandemic has become the most significant global health crisis of the 21st century, with a major challenge being the rapid diagnosis of infected individuals. This is crucial for effective isolation and isolation management. This study focuses on developing a double-layered classification system for accurately diagnosing COVID19 patients through the use of chest X-ray imaging, combining deep learning techniques with ensemble models. To achieve this, a cutting-edge pre-trained BERT-based 3D CNN architecture is presented, which extracts both global and local spatial features from input images. These features are then utilized in the first classification stage to distinguish between COVID19 and nonCOVID19 cases. The second stage involves an enhanced XGBoost classifier to differentiate between pneumonia and normal categories. To evaluate its effectiveness, the proposed model was tested on a comprehensive dataset of 13,500 chest X-ray images from the COVID19 database. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to existing single-stage classification systems.

Network science has grown into a widely recognized and applied field, with breakthroughs often relying on computational tools to analyze real-world networks. The emergence of open-source software has facilitated the development of novel analytical techniques and methods to tackle complex network challenges. Despite this, many network scientists and aspirants may not be familiar with industry-standard tools and resources, a gap this article aims to address by providing a comprehensive overview of essential software packages, online tools, books, courses, conferences, and professional organizations available to the network science community.

The study of eco-evolutionary dynamics is a complex process involving multiple factors, from evolutionary mechanisms to ecological feedback loops. These dynamics can be influenced by various factors, including natural selection, genetic drift, and resource availability. These mechanisms can operate on vastly different timescales, making it challenging to study their interactions. Our understanding of these dynamics is further complicated by their potential impact on ecosystems and evolutionary processes. These findings have significant implications for fields such as conservation biology and evolutionary medicine. Our review highlights the diverse theoretical and methodological approaches used to study eco-evolutionary dynamics, emphasizing the need for interdisciplinary collaboration. Our analysis reveals that eco-evolutionary dynamics are shaped by a complex interplay of biological and ecological mechanisms, with the potential for rapid and significant changes. Our findings suggest that eco-evolutionary dynamics can have profound implications for understanding and predicting the outcomes of conservation efforts in medicine and biology.

A recently proposed speech learning technique that operates without supervision has shown significant potential in improving speech recognition accuracy when combined with existing speech models. However, research into the effects of intentionally introduced distortions on this learning technique remains limited. We investigated the susceptibility of a speech denoising task to distortions used in attacks and discovered that certain distortion types, like those intended for speech enhancement, can significantly degrade the performance of the depth features it generates when subjected to hostile environments. Furthermore, we discovered that the decrease in performance is not solely due to the accumulation of distortion effects but is largely attributed to the cross-category confusion of distorted speech samples during training. To address this issue, we developed an innovative method for incorporating speech data that effectively mitigates the impact of distorted speech, thereby significantly improving the precision of the model when used with existing speech models even after an attack.

The emergence of decentralized exchanges on the blockchain has the potential to transform the traditional cryptocurrency trading system by offering greater accessibility and anonymity. Our research focuses on the key factors influencing consumers to adopt blockchain-based DEXs and uses data from 336 Chinese users to validate a comprehensive model of technology adoption. Our findings indicate that perceived usefulness, ease of use, and compatibility values significantly impact consumers' decisions to adopt blockchain-based DEXs. Our results also reveal that the effects of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and compatibility are mediated by consumers' attitudes towards the technology. Our study provides valuable insights into the field of technology management and sheds light on the benefits of adopting blockchain-based DEXs.

A new analytical framework is introduced to determine sensitivity to imputing missing data in Bayesian meta-analyses that involve effect sizes. The methodology utilizes the E-value, originally designed to gauge confounding bias, to account for bias introduced by missing effect sizes in a meta-analysis. The proposed framework generates sensitivity curves that assign probabilities in the effect size distribution, thereby quantifying the strength of non-missing effects relative to one another. This allows for the investigation of hypothetical scenarios where strong, non-missing effects diverge from the included moderators' predictions. Our framework demonstrates that conditional on observed data and moderators' predictions, the magnitude of bias in conditional imputations is typically negligible. Furthermore, a simulation study is conducted to evaluate the performance of the framework in detecting a set of relevant effect size moderators.

This study concludes a comprehensive classification of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-symmetries for the extended quantum plane $\mathbb{C}\left\langle x,y\right\rangle$, previously introduced by the author in a related paper.

The integration of Artificial Intelligence in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) is transforming the automotive industry by enabling contextual awareness and facilitating seamless communication between connected vehicles. As a result, AI models can be trained on local model parameters and shared with other vehicles to improve overall system performance. However, data privacy concerns and security risks pose significant challenges in achieving this goal. To address these challenges, Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising solution, allowing AI models to be trained on distributed datasets while ensuring data privacy. To mitigate security risks, blockchain technology can provide a secure and transparent framework for coordinating FL in IoV. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of blockchain-enabled FL in IoV, discussing various use cases, challenges, and potential research directions to facilitate future advancements in this area.

The ALICE experiment at the LHC measured the production of D mesons in proton-proton collisions at a higher energy of 5.02 TeV. The measurements cover a wide pseudorapidity range and are based on both direct and entirely produced D mesons. The results are the first to cover a high-energy range and are the first to be based on a higher energy collisions. The production cross sections are compared with theoretical predictions to understand the mechanisms of quark fragmentation and parton interactions.

The growing number of quantum computing technologies requires larger and larger cooling systems to accommodate research and testing.  The 16000 square foot platform at Fermilab's Quantum Information Science Center at the National Scientific User Facility is uniquely suited to accommodate large-scale cryogenic environments.  This paper describes the latest additions to this facility, a highly advanced and highly modular testing environment now capable of housing extremely large experiments at extremely low temperatures.  This expansive platform boasts 16 highly-stacked cryogenic systems, with extremely precise temperature control and the ability to integrate with external experimental equipment.  This cutting-edge environment, with its highly customizable features, provides an ideal setting for research and testing of a wide variety of emerging quantum computing technologies, including superconducting circuits, superconducting circuits with microwave input/output, and other quantum systems.

Previous research has highlighted the prevalence of misused cryptographic tools in Java applications. This study aims to provide an overview of the frequent incorrect uses of cryptographic tools in Python code. Additionally, the paper delves into the common security vulnerabilities associated with these incorrect uses and compares the Python environment to its Java counterpart, highlighting similarities and disparities.

This paper introduces a new approach to automatically labeling large-scale
urban scene datasets, which is crucial for developing advanced computer vision
applications. Our method, called Voting-based Automatic Labeling for Urban Scenes
and Environments, utilizes a grid-based system to divide the dataset into smaller
segments, which are then assigned labels through a combination of grid-based
neighbor relationships and a randomized labeling process. Our experiments on
large datasets demonstrate that this approach is both efficient and accurate,
outperforming existing methods while also providing a nearly ten-fold increase in
labeling speed compared to a widely-used urban dataset.

We introduce a new class of sparse models, the nonuniform sparse model, and develop a proximal average network (ProSPAN) designed to generate this specific class of models. ProSPAN combines learned calibrations for the $l_1$ and $l_2$ proximal averages, achieved by training on labeled data. We then apply the network to reflectivity inversion in seismic data, and through simulations, demonstrate that the nonuniform sparse model outperforms the uniformly sparse model in addressing seismic dispersion. Our results show the ProSPAN network can accurately calibrate the unique sparsity patterns of each channel, and when applied to field data, it yields sparsity patterns consistent with geological expectations.

This study examines the behavior of iterated semigroups of composition operators on BMOA-type spaces, where we derive integral operator representations for nth preimages. Additionally, we investigate under what conditions the set of nth preimages is finite-dimensional and explore the interaction between composition operators and integral operators in the given context.

We have developed a method to determine universal scaling functions for critical two-dimensional systems with a specific type of four-point correlation function. Our approach relies on calculating overlaps of ground states in finite systems at long distances, which can be implemented numerically using matrix product states. By combining this information with a basic rescaling argument, we can accurately identify critical exponents and universal functions for this type of correlation function. Our results are supported by exact calculations using conformal field theory and demonstrate that this method is an efficient tool for analyzing systems that are difficult to study using traditional techniques. We have applied this technique to the Haagerup topological quantum field theory to calculate the dimensions of certain primary fields and their associated mutual central charges.

To accommodate the variability in historical language data, we developed a novel part-of-speech tagging algorithm that assigns tags as sets of potential labels, rather than a single label. This approach, combined with a character-based neural network, allows us to handle ambiguous or previously unseen words commonly found in older texts. We evaluated the effectiveness of our algorithm on 99,548 historically significant German religious texts from the 15th to 16th centuries and found it outperformed traditional single-label methods in terms of accuracy and consistency. This approach has significant implications for broader historical language analysis and translation tasks.

This research focuses on developing a method to calculate a utility function's lower bound, given that it has a non-differentiable form and multiple arguments. A utility function's coherence is defined as its monotonicity, sub-additivity, and closure to logical combinations. The research also investigates the conditions for a utility function to be measurable and demonstrates that conditions for a utility function to be lower-bounded are distinct from those for it to be bounded from below. Furthermore, the research establishes that a utility function is lower-bounded if and only if it is measurable and semi-proper, with semi-properness being defined as the condition for a utility function to be lower-bounded with its own arguments, and we demonstrate that semi-properness is a form of weak-coherence. Finally, the research discusses the conditions for a utility function to be lower-bounded if and only if it is semi-continuous from below, with a focus on the case where a utility function is bounded from below if and only if it is lower-hemicontinuous and semi-proper, with a further demonstration that lower-hemicontinuity is equivalent to semi-continuity from below for certain classes of coherent utility functions.

This study presents an innovative software tool designed to automatically translate city development requirements into a formal specification using the CityREng framework.
City engineers supply basic city development requirements, which the tool interprets and converts into structured formal specifications.
City development requirements often involve complex interconnections and ambiguities.
To address this, the study incorporates a combination of techniques, including natural language processing, knowledge graphs, and a chat-based interface.
An experimental evaluation involving 10 subjects demonstrated the tool's effectiveness in accurately converting text-based requirements into formal specifications with 80% accuracy.
Additionally, the study highlights the tool's capacity to enhance its internal knowledge base through machine learning methods.

As quantum devices become more complex, the issue of intrinsic errors becomes increasingly significant. These devices typically lack the capability to tolerate quantum errors, which severely restricts their use. To address this challenge, alternative methods to full quantum error correction have been explored, with the hidden inverses protocol being one of the most promising approaches. This involves reversing the effect of an error by applying the inverse of the error-prone gate, which can be approximated by compiling it into a sequence of gates that effectively cancel out the error's effect. This paper demonstrates the feasibility of the hidden inverses protocol on a superconducting quantum device, achieving error cancellation with an accuracy of 90% through the use of a randomized Pauli decomposition. This research represents the first successful implementation of the hidden inverses protocol on a superconducting quantum device, paving the way for further developments in quantum error mitigation.

In a general category $\mathbb E$, the operation that takes a subobject $i$ of a given object $A$, and finds its "largest" version $i^\dagger$ within $A$, after being re-embedded into it cocartesianly, does not always exist. This particular feature is absent in categories like $(\mathbf{Rel}, \times)$, but does exist in categories like $(\mathbf{Posets}, \times)$, as well as in all exact categories. This study investigates under what conditions this operation $i\mapsto i^\dagger$ exists on categories that are regular but not necessarily exact. This study specifically looks at how this feature applies to categories that are obtained by localising to a set of monomorphisms, and presents an example of a category in which the operation $i\mapsto i^\dagger$ exists, but is not fully extendable to an exact category.

The application of statistical co-sampling techniques to analyzing multi-dimensional extreme events in the ocean has grown significantly in recent years. Multi-dimensional spatial models focusing on conditional extreme events can effectively capture observed patterns of interdependence among neighboring locations. This article demonstrates how such models can be applied to a dataset comprising extreme ocean environments across multiple locations in the Western North Atlantic, thereby highlighting their practical value.

Recently, Contrative Learning (CL) pre-training has shown great potential in creating versatile image understanding models for various downstream tasks. However, the performance of CL-based models is compromised when dealing with text inputs containing text disruptions, such as misspellings. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a new approach, VT-CLIP, which integrates CL and our novel visual-guided text module to improve the handling of disrupted text. Specifically, VT-CLIP's visual-guided text module leverages visual context to suggest probable correct text, utilizing visual features and a learned visual-guided model. Moreover, VT-CLIP's pre-training process combines our proposed learning objectives, including visual-guided text contrastive loss, to effectively capture and interpret text and visual information. Experimental results on various benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of VT-CLIP, including a 3.8% improvement in COCO Captioning and a 9.2% improvement in WICAR on Caption Degradation.

To efficiently handle noisy matrix equations, we develop a new approach called Operator Shifting for Multiscale Noisy Matrix Systems (OS-MSNMS). This approach solves each matrix individually, thereby reducing the computational complexity. By transforming the original system into its equivalent noisy form, we can leverage existing iterative solution methods. To further optimize performance, we establish criteria for convergence and introduce the concept of Optimal Noisy Operator Shifts. This concept is then applied to Gaussian noise to yield specific Best Positive Definite Shifts. To validate our theory, we implement and test our proposed method on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

We calculate the slices and the slice spectral sequence of integral suspensions of the equivariant Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra, where the spectra of the form $H\mathbb{Q}$, $\mathbb{R}H\mathbb{F}_p$, and $\mathbb{C}H\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$ are the focus, considering the action of the equivariant group $C_2$. Our investigation yields the integral equivariant homology of the equivariant homotopy groups, ultimately allowing us to resolve the problem of equivariant homotopy groups for the equivariant wedges involving the equivariant Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra.

Given a Noetherian local ring with a specific prime characteristic, we've developed criteria to establish F-rationality based on the tightness of its Hilbert function and polynomial. The results are further extended to broader scenarios, including semi-local complete integer rings and varieties of positive dimension prime characteristic, defined with a specific canonical module and non-pathological behavior. The study identifies and compares existing conditions for tightness, including local settings and projective scenarios, ultimately linking F-rationality to global properties. The study also explores the relationship between the tightness of a ring's completion and its original form.

The incorporation of high-dimensional machine learning outputs in medical imaging, such as those from digital pathology and radiology, is becoming increasingly significant. To address the need for seamless data exchange between healthcare providers and researchers, the DICOM standard has been developed. Although the standard initially focused on imaging, it has now incorporated specific modules for healthcare data, including the HighPerformanceModelResult module, which caters to medical imaging model outputs. However, the lack of practical tools has hindered the widespread adoption of these modules in the medical and research communities. To bridge this gap, the authors have developed a Python library called highdicom, which streamlines the annotation and model output encoding process by adhering to DICOM and HighPerformanceModelModel standards. This paper showcases the features of highdicom, demonstrating its capabilities in digital pathology and radiology, and illustrates its efficiency in creating outputs compliant with the HighPerformanceMedicalImagingDataStructure, Part 10 of DICOM Part 4.

We present a derivation of Noether's current for the surface term of Einstein-Hilbert action. The resulting Noether charge two-form is shown to yield a Virasoro algebra under the appropriate canonical transformation of a diffeomorphism vector field. This process also reveals that the entropy of a non-extremal black hole can be expressed as the entanglement entropy associated with its event horizon, corresponding to a surface term. A diffeomorphism vector field satisfying specific boundary conditions is identified, along with a corresponding surface term cutoff surface. The entropy of such a surface is found to be equivalent to the entanglement entropy associated with the event horizon, a key insight in understanding holographic duality.

In recent years, deep learning models have gained significant attention in analyzing DNA sequences, particularly in the field of genomics. A recent study by Dunn et al. employed a deep learning approach to pinpoint regulatory elements within DNA sequences by creating a neural network that could learn and recognize patterns in DNA representations automatically. This paper continues their work by introducing a novel, end-to-end trainable neural network that utilizes a convolutional layer to create a unified embedding space for DNA sequences, enabling further analysis and comparison.

The phase transition between metal and insulator states in V$_2$O$_3$ is highly influenced by its crystal structure, making the metal-insulator transition sensitive to such changes. In this study, we investigate the phase transition between the metal-like and insulating states in V$_2$O$_3$ ultrathin films on a sapphire substrate using various experimental techniques. Our results demonstrate that films with the same termination phase as the bulk insulating phase exhibit an insulating state, while those with the opposite phase exhibit a metal-like state. Furthermore, through first-principles calculations, we confirm the structural differences between the two phases and show that these differences can be attributed to the differing positions of vanadium atoms. Our findings provide new insights into the complex nature of the metal-insulator phase transition in V$_2$O$_3$ and its dependence on structural features.

A new, systematic method called "clebsch canonization" provides a general procedure to convert Lie-Poisson equations into a simplified canonical form characterized by two sets of conjugate variables. It's based on a previously developed technique in [2], which found a transformation to the canonical form using a specific Lie-Poisson matrix structure, now referred to as the "generalized kinetic momenta theorem." The current paper presents an alternative, more universal approach to this theorem and demonstrates the method by converting the rigid body Lie-Poisson equations into a canonical form, yielding the traditional Hamilton's equations.

We have compiled a comprehensive list of 443 exoplanets identified through the detection of prime-caused anomalies in the 2018 data from the KMTNet survey, bringing the total number of planets discovered by this method to 447. Out of these, 42 are new discoveries, bringing the total number of KMTNet discovered exoplanets to 447. We have used statistical analysis to determine the underlying population of these planets, revealing that the majority of them are long-period Neptune-sized objects, with the majority of them being located in the prime-caused field, although the results from the sub-prime survey are consistent with the earlier findings. We have also successfully identified four additional TRAPPIST-1-like multi-planet systems, bringing the total number of such systems to a total of seven, and highlighting the importance of continuous transit timing variation monitoring of stars hosting multiple planets to understand the underlying population of these planets, particularly those that are in resonance.

A key feature of Hamiltonian systems like fluid dynamics equations is their possession of conserved quantities. By introducing specific transformations to these conservation laws, researchers can effectively modify the behavior of systems and enhance their controllability. This method was recently demonstrated to work on compressible Navier-Stokes equations, where it helped resolve a long-standing issue by showing that certain boundary conditions can indeed lead to convergence to equilibrium.

A loan default prediction task involves assessing the likelihood of a borrower failing to meet repayment obligations after signing a loan contract. To address this problem, machine learning models were applied to a loan dataset, and the effectiveness of these models was compared. Furthermore, the importance of various loan features was analyzed using three distinct methodologies.

The concept of q-analogues of Dyck paths originates from the work of Stanley in 1995, specifically tied to the properties of lattice permutations. These q-analogues are defined by the sum of products of q-power differences corresponding to the exponents in the chromatic symmetric functions of path configurations within the associated Young tableaux. The resultant polynomials are found to be symmetric and dependent on the shape of the associated Young tableaux, the number of Dyck paths equal to the hook-length of a particular partition. The Hall-Littlewood polynomials of shapes (r,1) are determined to be equal to the q-Dyck path sums. Additionally, the relationships between q-Dyck paths and r-quotients of partitions, as well as r-Dyck paths, are explored and compared with the theory of q-Dyck paths established by Garsia and Remmel in 1991.

Deep learning models, specifically Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs),
have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in image classification tasks.
However, these networks often struggle with small variations in local features,
resulting in a need for data augmentation to enhance their performance.
In this paper, we introduce the Orientation Convolution (ORC) filter, a novel
convolutional filter designed to enhance DCNNs' image classification
performance by automatically invariating local features to their orientation.
The ORC filter achieves this by stacking multiple Regular Convolution (RCC)
filters and combining their outputs to create an invariant response.
We evaluate the ORC filter on two benchmark datasets: CIFAR-10 and
Stl10-10k, and observe significant improvements in the DCNN's ability to
classify orientations without the need for data augmentation, yielding better
accuracy and higher efficiency.
Our findings suggest that the ORC filter offers a general approach to
optimizing the ORC-DCNN for various image classification tasks.

Using a novel relative trace formula, we investigate linear periods on $GL_{2n}$ that are modulated by a character. The key elements in this process involve establishing the relative fundamental lemma and the orbital integral decomposition, which ultimately leads to the derivation of the meromorphic continuation of zeta integrals. As a direct result, we prove algebraic congruence subgroups of $Sp_{2n}$ possess nonvanishing automorphic forms.

We develop a systematic method to study the impact of mass on the pole mass in
quantum field theories, specifically in Standard Model-like scenarios with varying
numbers of light massive flavors. Our method leverages the properties of threshold
resummation and flavor evolution to derive a universal relationship between the pole
mass and the running mass, valid across all flavors. This allows for a model-independent
assessment of the pole mass's sensitivity to flavor variations. Our results are applied
to the Standard Model, revealing that the mild variation in the running mass of light
quarks leads to a negligible shift in the pole mass, amounting to approximately 20 MeV.
This value is comparable to current direct electroweak measurements and significantly
exceeds the current direct top quark mass measurement accuracy.

A specific type of vertex-coloring known as an edge-coloring on regular graphs has been studied extensively, particularly in relation to a problem first posed by Erdos and Gall regarding the minimum number of colors needed for such colorings in order to avoid adjacent edges having the same color. This problem has been further explored by other researchers, such as Galaz-Garcia et al., who investigated rainbow connections in regular graphs, requiring the minimum number of colors to ensure that there is a path with all distinct colors. In contrast, a variant known as an strong edge-coloring, introduced by Borodin, imposes the condition that all distinct colors are required even if vertices connected by an edge are not directly linked. More recently, a new problem referred to as precoloring extension, introduced by Feder, was explored, involving the scenario where colors are only assigned to some vertices and the goal is to extend this color assignment to all vertices while minimizing the total number of colors used. This problem has been shown to be closely related to other well-known graph coloring problems, such as vertex-coloring, and has been explored in various studies. In this paper, we investigate the strong edge-coloring variant of the problem, focusing on regular graphs and showing that, for such graphs, the minimum number of colors required for such colorings is at most the maximum degree plus the square root of the maximum degree, a significant improvement on previous bounds.
We establish a precise relationship between L^p to L^q contraction inequalities in the L^p( L^q(0,1) ) space and the same contraction in the weighted Bergman space Q_p(0,1).

A highly contagious and deadly form of pneumonia called COVID-19 has become a global pandemic, with a COVID-19 diagnostic tool called CT scans being widely used. Although CT scans are typically high-quality, they produce large datasets that take a long time to analyze, making them less suitable for emergency situations. As a result, researchers have been looking for a way to obtain accurate diagnoses from lower-quality, faster scans. A new, two-stage approach using a time-distributed capsule network has been proposed to process low-quality CT scans quickly and accurately. This approach outperforms other methods in terms of accuracy and diagnosis time, achieving a 93.2% success rate and 0.133 seconds for image classification, 0.001 seconds for image detection, and 0.002 seconds for image segmentation.

As more people become reliant on satellite technology, there is a growing concern for the sustainability of the geocentric orbit. This has sparked interest in assessing the density and distribution of space debris in the vicinity of Earth's surface. This study employs a statistical framework rooted in spatial point patterns to model the arrangement of debris in the geocentric orbit. By applying this framework, researchers have developed a novel approach to evaluate and analyze the spatial distribution of debris, with a particular focus on its radial and angular patterns. This has led to the development of a new index for measuring the density of debris, known as the nearest neighbor ratio. Furthermore, the framework enables the comparison of debris density at a particular point with its average density, as well as the comparison of debris density patterns between two distinct datasets. This framework has been applied to a dataset of approximately 30,000 objects in the geocentric orbit with an inclination of less than 90 degrees, and the results indicate that debris follows a non-random pattern, characterized by clustering.

High-order unstructured meshes are being increasingly utilized in Computational Fluid Dynamics simulations due to their superior accuracy. However, the current technology for generating high-order unstructured meshes on complex CAD models is lacking. We propose a novel method to automatically create high-order quadrilateral elements for 3D CAD models, which can then be employed to generate high-quality tetrahedral meshes. Our approach involves using integer linear programming to optimize the creation of a high-order quadrilateral mesh from a 3D CAD model. The method is validated on various models and compared to a recent 3D mesher that generates higher quality finer meshes.

Pearson's correlation coefficient is widely used in various fields to measure linear relationships between two continuous variables. However, interpreting results can be challenging without visual aids, especially when analyzing datasets through random permutations, common in hypothesis testing. This study provides analytical formulas for the moments of permutation-based correlation coefficients, enabling researchers to gain deeper insights into its behavior during statistical tests.

We detail the reasoning behind implementing a quantum S-matrix framework for tackling classical gravitational scattering between two bodies. Furthermore, a method is briefly discussed for computing black hole metrics across multiple spatial dimensions.

This research aims to determine the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the controlled Navier-Stokes equations, specifically in a three-dimensional domain with smooth boundaries. The goal of this work is to prove that these solutions can be stabilized through finite-dimensional feedback controls that localize within the domain, using a method developed by Guo and Li in their previous research, which focused on the controlled Navier-Stokes equations in the entire three-dimensional space. The existence of global solutions, even with initial values in critical Sobolev spaces, has been established in this study. The research further employs the Baire ordinal method to establish the property of finite dimensionality in the inner domain and demonstrates its effectiveness through the use of Riesz basis along with a unique continuation property for the Stokes semigroup. The research presents its findings through the use of Besov and Sobolev spaces, which are adapted to accommodate the specific characteristics of the controlled Navier-Stokes equations.

Language learning dictionaries play a crucial role in helping learners grasp the nuances of vocabulary, particularly for languages like Chinese, which has a vast character set. This study introduces the LitMind Dictionary, a freely accessible online dictionary with an extensive collection of Classical Chinese entries, which can be accessed at https://www.litmind.com/dictionary. Furthermore, the data set is also available for download, enabling further research, and its website includes functionality to visualize characters using the LitMind Dictionary.

The growing interest in explaining recommender systems stems from a desire to increase transparency and trust, as well as a need for fairness and accountability. However, post-explanation methods like LIME and SHAP have limitations, particularly in their ability to provide clear and actionable insights into specific items and users. A new set of evaluation metrics, Adherence and Constancy, have been introduced to assess the quality of local and global explanations in these systems. Analysis through two real-world datasets reveals that Adherence and Constancy are correlated and provide valuable, albeit distinct, perspectives on the explainability of recommendation models.

Quantum devices based on superconducting and semiconductor materials require precise surface control. The interface between these materials and their surface layers is critical. The proximity effect between a superconductor and a semiconductor allows for the creation of novel phenomena and devices. The proximity effect enables the flow of Cooper pairs and the creation of Kondo states in quantum dots. The semiconductor's thickness and Fermi level positioning are key factors in achieving this, but the surface states interfere with these processes. The interface between InAs quantum wells and their AlInAs barrier layers is a promising device platform, but the surface states in InAs quantum devices cause unwanted electron accumulation. The electron accumulation at the surface shifts the energy levels and affects the device's performance. Theoretical models suggest that the accumulation is caused by the surface states of InAs, but experimental evidence is lacking. The surface states of InAs are not fully understood and controlling the surface electron accumulation is a significant challenge. The electron accumulation at the surface can be controlled by the deposition of a thin layer of InAs and then annealing the layer to remove the excess electrons. The electron accumulation at the surface can be further controlled by the application of an electric field and the use of a top contact. The electron accumulation at the surface can be minimized by the use of a thin layer of InAs and a top contact. The electron accumulation at the surface can be controlled by the use of a thin layer of InAs and a top contact. The electron accumulation at the surface can

This paper investigates the query complexity of learning concepts that are robust against adversarial changes. Our results show that in order to learn any concept conceptually robust by a margin $\epsilon$ while tolerating an error rate $\delta$, one must make $2^{O(1/\epsilon)}$ local queries to the training data. In comparison, if the concept's overall robustness is taken into account, robust learning can be achieved through non-local adaptive queries with an error rate of $\delta$. These findings highlight the significant challenge of designing learning algorithms that are both efficient and robust.

Our previous research introduced an accurate and efficient method for calculating Sinkhorn iterates, specifically fast $ST_k(b,a)$ that converges linearly to a $k$-digit accurate solution for optimizing transport. This paper builds upon that work by developing a new algorithm, referred to as EFTLK, which achieves even greater speed and accuracy in a single process. We outline this method's steps, prove its convergence, compare its performance with other approaches, and provide various experiments to illustrate its effectiveness.

Young stars emit far-ultraviolet radiation that significantly influences the evolution of nearby protoplanetary disks and the atmospheric development of forming planets. To better understand the impact of these radiation sources, we analyzed the behavior of the young star AU Mic, specifically focusing on its quiescent and flare states. By using the Far Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Explorer, we obtained new observations of AU Mic's quiescent emission and found it to be FUV-luminous, with the majority of energy coming from neutral atomic and molecular metals in the upper atmosphere of its stellar corona. These findings suggest that white dwarf planets in the system AU Mic could be heated to high temperatures, with the potential for their atmospheres to be significantly affected.

This study examines the friction experienced by an accelerating charged particle moving through a non-stationary dielectric medium. The medium is modeled as a material with a dielectric constant and is analyzed using the Iliopoulos-Kaplanov-Tavkhelidze (IKT) method. The medium's nonlinearity leads to a drag force, or friction, that arises from the interaction between the charged particle and the dielectric's polarization field. Notably, this friction is non-zero only when the charged particle moves at speeds comparable to or faster than the phase velocity of light in the dielectric's rest frame. In the extreme case of ultra-relativistic motion, this friction is inversely proportional to the dielectric constant.

In the context of an unevenly distributed classification problem, the area of
minimum risk minimization (MMRM) has received limited attention. This study derives
a statistical approach for MMRM using the nearest neighbor classification rule,
providing a solution for handling imbalanced datasets.

We have identified 20 Ultra-Luminous Quasars (ULQs) with absolute $g$-band magnitudes brighter than $-24.5$, using SkyMapper data and quasar-like spectra from follow-up observations, including spectroscopy from the ANU 2.3m telescope and VLT. Our sample, when combined with existing ULQs from the Quasar Hypersurvey, covers a range of redshifts from 1.8 to 3.1, with the majority being newly discovered. We have combined our complete ULQ catalog to create a new luminosity function, which is the most comprehensive ULQ study to date, covering the full redshift range from 1.5 to 3.1. Our findings indicate that ULQs are rare, with a space density of approximately $10^{-7}$ Mpc$^{-3}$, and that their luminosity follows a power law with a slope of around 3.1. We have also estimated the cosmic star formation rate contribution of ULQs, which is approximately 15-20% at $z=2$.

We've developed a groundbreaking experimental technique to detect tunneling events on a quantum dot that is connected to a superconducting island, all while observing the system's charge sensing behavior simultaneously. This novel setup, implemented using aluminum islands and gates, enables us to monitor the system's electrostatic properties and charge tunneling in real-time. This unique combination of properties offers new insights into the fundamental behavior of superconducting islands and allows for the discovery of previously unknown phenomena, such as the distinct differences in energy levels of the system's even and odd charge states.

Our research reveals that in systems of conservation laws, an entropic discontinuity can exist even when there's no classical shock solution that satisfies the Riemann problem. Conversely, under certain conditions on the flux function, such entropic solutions are possible only if they align with a contractions criterion and, in certain cases, the classical shock solution does exist and is unique. Our findings hinge on a novel approach involving the contraction metric method to assess stability and entropy inequalities.

We present a novel view generation challenge called DiffDreamer, which focuses on maintaining consistency while creating a 3D scene from a single image's perspective changes. Our approach, DiffDreamer, utilizes a novel 3D conditional diffusion model trained end-to-end to generate dynamic, immersive scenes from a single input image. Unlike existing methods, DiffDreamer's training data is easily obtainable from static images and its evaluation is independent of any image translation techniques. Our novel approach's effectiveness and adaptability are showcased through various real-world applications, demonstrating its potential for future research and practical use.

This paper presents a new, data-driven approach to predicting and solving complex dynamic systems connected through networks. These systems can represent real-world processes, such as the spread of diseases or chemical reactions. A new method is introduced to estimate the behavior of each connection based on measurable data. Using this method, it's possible to forecast the behavior of a system even when the behavior of individual connections is unknown. This knowledge is then applied to tackle a complex process planning challenge known as Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming. By applying this approach to a specific model of disease spread, our results show that the new method successfully provides accurate predictions and an optimal solution for determining the best course of action to manage the disease.

The dynamics of a liquid film on a fiber, influenced by surface tension, were examined in a study that considered the liquid's motion relative to the surrounding air. The researchers found that the behavior of the liquid film undergoes a transition from stable to unstable based on the difference in viscosity between the liquid and air. When the liquid is more viscous than air, the film becomes unstable and breaks down into droplets, but as the air's viscosity increases, a range of unstable wavelengths of perturbations can emerge, leading to the development of lumps. In the case of a liquid surrounded by air, the instabilities are enhanced, and the liquid film breaks down into droplets and gas pockets, forming a two-phase structure. In contrast, when the air is the less viscous phase, the instability is delayed, and the liquid film breaks down into alternating sections of larger and smaller droplets, leading to a unique pattern.

We investigate the temporal Lipschitz stability for solutions of the Hunter-Saxton equation, focusing on $\alpha$-dissipative solutions with $\alpha$ a constant in the interval $[0,1]$. We introduce and study the properties of metrics both in the Lagrangian and Eulerian frameworks to determine Lipschitz stability within those systems.

Evaluating scoliosis through ultrasound is a reliable process that can be done manually, but it has a problem - different people may get different results. Using robots to scan patients could help solve this issue by providing consistent results. Our study aimed to understand how consistent robotic ultrasound images are in the spine and how reliable they are compared to manual scans. We did this by having five different people scan the same 10 scoliosis cases and comparing their results with a robot that was guided along the spine. We found that the robotic scans produced consistent results and were just as accurate as manual scans in determining the curvature of the spine. This discovery opens up the possibility of using robots to automatically and consistently scan the spine in the future.

This paper introduces an innovative method for creating synthetic speech duration models using a non-parametric approach, eliminating the need for complex parametric assumptions. Median values are used instead of mean values to minimize the impact of outliers, and the proposed approach allows for the creation of more realistic synthetic speech by accurately mirroring the duration distributions of real speech.

A rising trend in the proliferation of social networking platforms has facilitated the proliferation of hate speech, a public discourse bane.  Given the limitations of resource availability, hate speech monitoring on social media is proving insurmountable for human moderators.  The emergence of automated hate speech detection on social media content has garnered significant attention.  The study of hate speech on the NLP community has gained significant traction, with the recent exploration of the toxicity of the social media content on the XAI-18K dataset.  The study presents a feature extraction-based framework for hate speech detection on the XAI-18K dataset, demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed model with the highest performance compared to the state-of-the-art.  The study's comprehensive analysis of the task and the high-performance of the proposed model are notable contributions.

Multi-input multi-output (MIMO) networks, a prominent deep learning architecture, are designed to expedite learning and enhance performance by rapidly combining and sharing features. Despite its potential, a typical MIMO architecture often exhibits subpar performance and a failure to converge, which severely restricts its practical applications. This paper presents a comprehensive study of the critical issues hindering efficient feature sharing in MIMO networks, offering valuable insights for future research. Specifically, it delves into the challenges associated with feature resolution, dimensionality, and the design of MIMO modules, ultimately providing a set of practical guidelines for constructing high-performance MIMO networks.

The analysis and interpretation of ancient texts and manuscripts rely heavily on accessible, comprehensive collections of digitized images, which serve as the foundation for advancements in related research. Through thorough examination and analysis, researchers can build upon existing knowledge and drive innovation within the field of historical document understanding. Unfortunately, a comprehensive database of such resources is lacking, prompting the need for a detailed survey to fill this gap. This study provides a thorough overview of available datasets for ancient texts and manuscripts, which will serve as a valuable resource for improving related machine learning models and maintaining transparency among researchers.

This research focuses on developing a novel, efficient feedback control approach for industrial robots by leveraging the spinning wheel design of the joint. The proposed strategy leverages non-minimum phase system characteristics, allowing the use of lower-cost and more affordable position sensors instead of costly and heavy torque sensors. It incorporates two cost-effective incremental encoders to measure back-coupling effects, providing the necessary data for designing the control law using the flatness-based technique. The proposed control approach exhibits superior performance in handling disturbances and modeling errors, as evidenced by simulation results.

The study explores how to analyze longitudinal data related to specific health conditions, such as cardiovascular disease or diabetes, which can exist in different states (healthy or unhealthy) and are often influenced by lifestyle factors. Our research introduces a new statistical method to estimate the likelihood of different events (like death or hospitalization) over time, while accounting for the natural progression of certain diseases. Our research indicates that individuals with a past myocardial infarction have an increased risk of hospitalization and premature death, and this risk is significantly affected by factors such as age, sex, and BMI, and varies depending on whether the individual is in a healthy or unhealthy state.

A complex approach has been established for evaluating the continuous electron density of molecules, particularly for systems with multiple centers and non-relativistic Coulomb interactions. This method involves developing an efficient quadrature scheme based on a customized three-dimensional grid. By utilizing the rapid convergence properties of the Poisson-Laplace series and strategically reducing its computational cost, the approach enables fast and accurate calculations. Key optimizations include pre-calculating basis functions on a grid and developing a compact two-center expansion. Furthermore, non-linear interactions are handled through adaptive recursive integration. When compared to conventional numerical methods, the approach achieves comparable results with significantly reduced computational requirements.

In a graph, a set of vertices is considered a metric dimension if, for every other vertex, its distance to these vertices matches the distance to itself. Research has shown that finding the minimum metric dimension of a graph as a function of its size or the minimum degree is an NP-complete problem. This paper investigates the parameterized complexity of the problem when considering feedback vertex set, vertex cover, feedback vertex number, and clique cover number as parameters. The main findings show that both the feedback vertex set and vertex cover parameters lead to hard problems, while the number-based parameters result in parameterized symmetric OR problems, and the difficulty can be reduced to constants depending on the specific parameter value.

A topological space X is classified as a directed space if it possesses a self-mapping power structure characterized by a semigroup S, which dictates that $X^{X_\lambda} = X_\lambda$ for each element $\lambda$ within S. This paper delves into the essential properties and characteristics of directed spaces, including their path-connectedness and one-wholeness. It also presents methods for constructing directed spaces through the quotienting of free spaces and investigates the behavior of directed spaces under various types of continuous mappings, followed by an analysis of their limits and sequential properties. In addition, this paper explores the dual space concepts in relation to directed spaces, including directed frames and frame spectra.

Past and future Earth climate conditions have been predicted to be
extremely warm, with high temperatures likely to be sustained for
thousands of years. This scenario, known as the hothouse Earth
hypothesis, suggests that the Earth's climate could become unstable and
shift into a warm state on its own. We have conducted experiments in our
research that show how small changes in the amount of solar energy reaching
the Earth can cause large and dramatic fluctuations in our hothouse climate
models. We found that the climate can become trapped in intense wet or dry
periods, lasting for thousands of years, similar to the way our modern
climate can change dramatically from day to day or season to season. The
climate's response to these small energy changes is non-linear, meaning
that a small increase in energy can lead to disproportionately large
changes in the climate. We also discovered that these extreme periods of
wetness and dryness can occur in a variety of Earth climate conditions,
including those that existed in the past, such as during hothouse periods
in the late Paleocene and Eocene. Our research highlights the need for
further study of how hothouse climates respond to small changes in energy,
as understanding these extreme periods of wetness and dryness could be key
to predicting the potential impacts of global warming on hothouse Earth
climate conditions.

We've established an action for expanding Yang-Mills theory into higher spins that mirrors the structure of Penrose's transform. This action exists within a self-interacting 3-dimensional supermanifold, leading to a self-dual equation equivalent in its classical sector to the self-dual Yang-Mills equation. A second, simpler supermanifold action we've developed also relates to the Yang-Mills equation through a Penrose-like transform.

The growing use of deep learning techniques in medical image classification is being hampered by the issue of label noise, which significantly affects model performance. To address this problem, researchers have developed Bayesian Network-based approaches to identify and correct label noise during data annotation. A recent study, employing medical imaging data, demonstrated the effectiveness of these methods in improving model performance. This research extends the existing work by incorporating multiple organs into the Bayesian Network, which accelerates the learning process and enhances the overall performance of the model. Additionally, our study investigates the impact of varying levels of label noise on model performance, discovering that BN-based methods are particularly effective in handling highly noisy datasets. Furthermore, our study evaluates the efficacy of BN-based data cleaning methods in conjunction with different machine learning models.

Consider a unit cube $Q$ in 8-dimensional Euclidean space and an interior subset $W$ defined as the space where the sum of each coordinate's absolute value does not exceed 5, along with the condition that $x_7$ and $x_8$ are within the interval $(-\frac{2}{3},\frac{2}{3})$. The Pinsker's inequality for the norm of an interpolation projector provides an upper limit for the norm of the projector $P$ in the cube $Q$, specifically, $\|P\| \le 36.56$.

A correlated random walk (CRW) is an extension of the simple random walk on a graph, where transitioning probabilities between adjacent nodes are influenced by external factors. In this paper, we introduce the concept of "characteristic CRW" and establish a determinant expression for its transition probability matrix in terms of this characteristic CRW, providing explicit examples to illustrate its application.

In a dynamically evolving computing environment, functions are often parameterized by time to incorporate contextual changes, a concept referred to as temporality. To model such functions within a single, non-recursive framework, we introduce a "clocked" definition method, allowing a function's behavior to be determined by both time and context. Although simple unrolling can lead to unmanageable expressions, our "clocked" definition approach facilitates a balanced representation of recursive functions, effectively separating the effects of temporal and contextual variables. This method is illustrated by implementing a clocked unroller and is subsequently demonstrated through the redefinition of time-dependent functions such as list insertion and array update.

The dynamics of wall turbulence exhibit a complex interplay between the large-scale organized motions and the smaller disordered fluctuations. To better understand and model wall turbulence, researchers have developed Coherent Structure-based models, which replace disordered fluctuations with the background flow and the residual fluctuations. However, the conventional CSC models have limitations in accurately predicting the turbulent features, particularly the instantaneous wall turbulence, due to their limited ability to capture the coherent structures. To address this issue, the authors propose integrating Reynolds stress models into the CSC framework and augmenting them with a data-driven approach to account for coherant structures. This approach involves training neural networks using direct numerical simulation data and testing the improved CSC-RS model against experimental measurements. The results indicate that the enhanced model significantly improves the accuracy of predicting the mean flow and turbulent quantities, and the incorporation of coherent structures in the turbulent fluctuations yields notable improvements over conventional Reynolds stress models.

In a specific "baby Skyrme" model in 1+1 dimensions, which has connections to the Born-Infeld theory, researchers have found and analyzed self-dual solitons. These solitons demonstrate a property where the force between them is attractive. Furthermore, when compared to the well-known Bogomolny-Prasad-Sommerfield equation, it's observed that the force equation for these self-dual solitons behaves similarly in a limited scenario.

For a three-dimensional Weyl semimetal model in a magnetic field aligned along the z-axis, our study examines the effect of an in-plane electric field, finding that it breaks time-reversal symmetry, resulting in Weyl nodes appearing in the momentum space. The presence of a magnetic field splits each Weyl node into an infinite set of subnodes, located at specific positions within a unit cell in the momentum space, a phenomenon known as the Hofstadter regime. Our analysis reveals two distinct types of Weyl nodes within this regime: one connected pair, located near the edges of the unit cell, and numerous subnodes that remain isolated. The research further investigates the characteristics of the Fermi arcs and bulk quasi-energy states, associated with the Weyl nodes, for both the connected and isolated arcs.

A novel nano antenna design has been developed for the efficient, bright, and directional emission of photons. The hybrid nano antenna structure combines a ring made of a specific material, called $Si$, with a vertical rod. By adjusting the rod's material properties, there is a specific point at which light can be efficiently emitted in all directions. This setup also exhibits strong resistance to the loss of emitted light due to its unique combination of materials. The theoretical basis for this innovation is the Lorentz model used to analyze and optimize the nano antenna's performance.

The phenomenon of shear-induced jamming in simple fluids, particularly granular matter, has been observed to exhibit unusual behavior, characterized by the lateral flow of the substance. This behavior has been linked to a counterintuitive increase in effective friction coefficient, known as anomalous screening. Although an anomalous screening theory has been proposed to explain this phenomenon, the theoretical predictions have not been empirically verified. In this study, we conducted experiments using granular matter and found that the friction coefficient exhibits a non-linear relationship with normal stress, characterized by a concave shape. Our numerical simulations confirmed the anomalous screening theory's prediction that the friction coefficient's variation is inversely proportional to the square root of the characteristic length scale. These findings provide strong empirical evidence supporting the anomalous screening theory and shed new light on the complex behavior of materials exhibiting friction.

Utilizing first-principles calculations, our research explores the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of silicene and Mn-decorated silicene substrates of hexagonal boron nitride. Hexagonal boron nitride's intrinsic buckling facilitates the preservation of spin-orbit coupling in Mn decorated silicene. We discovered that while pure silicene exhibits a metallic character, both Mn decorated silicene and pure Mn sheet demonstrate half-metallic properties with a magnetic moment of 5μB. Furthermore, interactions between Mn and the hBN substrate led to changes in the BN layers' band structure, transforming them from metallic to insulating. We specifically investigated the electronic properties of Mn decorated silicene substrates of hBN and found that the spin-up and spin-down components display distinct characteristics. The results reveal that the interaction between Mn and the hBN substrate significantly alters the spin texture.

The Sgr A East supernova remnant is located at the heart of the Milky Way galaxy, centered on the black hole, Sgr A*. To understand the formation of this remnant, researchers investigated three proposed sites for a nearby supernova explosion: (i) near the center of the Remnant, (ii) above it, and (iii) to the north-east. By examining X-ray and radio data, they found that above and north-east of the remnant, there are no significant X-ray emissions above 10 keV in 2018. Furthermore, there are no substantial 10 GHz radio emissions extending into the Remnant, ruling out the initial hypothesis. Instead, they found that a supernova that exploded 2.5 kiloparsecs above the Remnant, moving towards the south-west, would have its shock wave intersect with the Remnant at the end of 2017, aligning with observed data.

In machine learning, handling imbalanced datasets is a well-studied problem, with techniques such as oversampling being commonly applied to imbalanced classes. This paper focuses on oversampling methods for text classification, where we examine four methods: Borderline-SMOTE, SVM-SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE-R, and ADASYN, and evaluate their effectiveness in improving the performance of machine learning models on imbalanced datasets. Our research involves creating imbalanced datasets using the 20 Newsgroups and Wikipedia corpora, and testing the impact of oversampling on the performance of KNN, SVM, and Random Forest classifiers, with a comparison to a model trained on the original, unaltered dataset, and a baseline model without oversampling.

This study investigates the connections between local news coverage and the COVID-19 pandemic in the 50 largest U.S. markets between March 1, 2020, and January 31, 2021. Using an AI-driven method, news content was categorized into relevant topics, revealing patterns in relation to COVID-19 coverage. Key findings indicate a notable rise in COVID-related news output in the initial months of the pandemic, followed by a gradual decline. Notably, local news coverage of COVID-19 initially surpassed national news coverage of the same topic. In-depth investigations into COVID-19 deaths and illnesses in the markets were explored, and a significant correlation was discovered between COVID-19 deaths and local news coverage. Additionally, a significant inverse correlation was found between local news consumption and COVID-19 cases and deaths.

Simulating physical systems with a multipole expansion allows for the calculation of angular momentum conservation, a property validated in methods like the Fast Multipole Method and the Cartesian Tree. However, conventional FMP data structures are not inherently suited to represent angular momentum, despite its potential importance in research areas such as molecular dynamics and astrophysics. This research presents a novel approach, incorporating a shifted Cartesian tree, which enables accurate calculation of angular momentum at any level of the hierarchy. By establishing relations between angular momentum and position, a force, and a torque, conventional trees can be upgraded to support efficient computation and maintenance of these properties. This advancement is demonstrated with a detailed algorithmic description, ultimately allowing for the efficient maintenance of angular momentum in fast data structures.

The strategy of utilizing the $E1$-$M1$ amplitude in the Sasa-Dynko formalism to explain the longitudinal-to-transverse polarization transfer ratio $Q_{LT}$ in an electron-proton collision is analyzed and found to be flawed. This flaw arises from the incorrect application of the $E1$-$M1$ amplitude, which fails to accurately describe the experimental findings obtained from the JLab experiment. Furthermore, comparisons with lattice QCD and QCD sum rule predictions of proton magnetic moments indicate that these methods do not align with the implications of utilizing the $E1$-$M1$ amplitude for $M1$ matrix elements in protons.

In the field of machine learning, particularly with complex tasks, using a group of specialists with different knowledge can be beneficial. Each expert would use a unique set of parameters, and collectively, they would contribute to a group decision. By utilizing different representations, we can achieve a balance between the overall decision-making process and computational efficiency. We found that using different representations as data enhancement strategies can lead to more effective group decision-making, and we demonstrated the success of this method in a series of experiments involving different types of experts and representations.

A study of Higgs boson pair production linked to a vector boson in $pp$ collisions at 13 TeV using the ATLAS detector is presented. Higgs bosons are assumed to originate from the loop-induced gluon-fusion production mode and a vector boson fusion mode in association with a additional jet. A search is conducted in association with a $W$ boson decaying into electrons or muons and Higgs bosons either decaying into muons or into electrons. This search is performed with a dataset of 139 inverse femtobarns of 13 TeV $pp$ collisions recorded in 2015 and 2016. Higgs boson production in association with a vector boson is not found. Exclusion limits at a 95% confidence level are established in terms of the Higgs-boson production cross-section modified by the $\kappa_F$ factor, a parameter that represents the common scaling of the Higgs boson's fermionic couplings. This results in the most stringent exclusion limits on the $\kappa_F$-scaled Higgs boson and the SM Higgs boson and Z boson paired with a $W$ boson and $W$ decaying into leptons. Higgs boson production in association with a vector boson and a jet is also considered in this study. This results in the Higgs-boson and SM $W$ bos

We've successfully created a digital spin maser that operates on a specific type of storage, which is governed by quantum rules. By utilizing the digital storage provided by trapped ions, we can easily transfer their quantum states to a maser based on potassium-40, through the use of controlled interactions that involve exchanging photons. This process allows us to create superpositions and entangled states within the maser, which can then be studied in detail through detailed analysis of the maser's behavior. Our research shows that the Masers' dynamics are significantly influenced by the storage and transfer processes, which can be studied in greater detail through the use of quantum rules.

For K3 surfaces with an automorphism having a Siegel disk, the associated Picard number lies between zero and ten and must be an even integer. Conversely, we demonstrate that on K3 surface classes exhibiting classical or non-linear periodic behavior, the sum of the codimensions of the immediate attracting and attracting sectors equals either zero or a positive integer less than two times the period. The codemonsymmetry principle for K3 surfaces shows that the codemonsymmetry holds as well for the sum of the codimensions of the immediate attracting and attracting sectors. The codemonsymmetry also establishes that the associated Lehn number, representing the codimension of the immediate attracting sector, aligns with established bounds.

A neutralino is assumed to be the primary component of dark matter, with its limited ability to interact with Standard Model particles resulting in predominantly non-relativistic annihilation processes. This leads to predominantly indirect signals from dark matter annihilation, with gamma ray emissions being a significant consideration. Assuming the neutralino mass lies between several hundred GeV and a TeV, previous studies have constrained the relevant parameters based on gamma ray data from space-based observatories and ground-based telescopes. However, considering that the neutralino mass may be lower than previous estimates, we conducted a re-evaluation of the constraints on the neutralino parameters using recent data from the Fermi-LAT and H.E.S.S. observatories.

The main contribution of this study involves developing a highly efficient approximation scheme for estimating the genus of complex graph structures to a precise degree. Notably, the time complexity of this scheme is nearly linear, at $\tilde{O}(n^2)$. To achieve this goal, the research introduces an innovative reduction technique that transforms the genus approximation challenge into the sparse graph genus estimation problem, where only a constant number of vertices are involved per edge. Furthermore, the authors present another efficient solution to the sparse graph problem, utilizing the $\tilde{O}(n^2) $-time algorithm developed by Dujmović et al. (2019).

A stochastic Newton algorithm for distributed convex optimization tasks is proposed, which utilizes individual machine capabilities to calculate gradient and Hessian-vector products for the same shared objective.
This method's computational efficiency is enhanced by allowing each machine to independently obtain these products, minimizing overall computational costs.
Consequently, a new computational complexity metric is defined, taking into account both computational and communication expenses.
The complexity of the proposed algorithm is evaluated using this new metric and found to be superior to other methods in specific scenarios.

Our study presents an examination of the application of neural networks in detecting hate-speech within Hindi and Bengali languages through the use of zero-shot transfer learning. We have established a combined dataset of approximately 10,000 annotated samples for Hindi/Bengali, drawing from around 20,000 samples from multiple sources. Our 5-fold cross-validation analysis of a binary classification task revealed that BERT-based models outperformed other models. Notably, our data indicates that a model trained on Hindi was capable of accurately identifying hate-speech in Bengali and vice versa.
